ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right of the figure is a D flip-flop, the left input terminal is labeled D, and below there is a clock input CP/C1; the upper output on the right is labeled Q, and the lower output on the right with a small inversion circle is fed back by a wire to the logic gate on the left. The logic gate on the left is marked “&” internally, and its output terminal also has a small inversion circle, so it is a NAND gate. The two inputs of this NAND gate are respectively the external input A and \overline{Q^n} fed back from the inverted output of the flip-flop. Reasoning: The NAND gate output is connected to the D input of the D flip-flop, so D=\overline{A\cdot \overline{Q^n}}. The next state of the D flip-flop at the clock edge equals the D input, so Q^{n+1}=D. By De Morgan's law, \overline{A\cdot \overline{Q^n}}=\overline{A}+Q^n. Therefore the next state is Q^{n+1}=\overline{A}+Q^n.
